# ET Exclusive | Sunil Mittal’s next big bets: AI, cloud, space telecom and a billion Airtel users
ET Exclusive | Sunil Mittal’s next big bets: AI, cloud, space telecom and a billion Airtel users
By
Kiran Rathee
&
Vinay Pandey
, ET Bureau Last Updated: Nov 12, 2026, 11:00:00 PM IST
Synopsis
Sunil Mittal reflects on the Bharti Group's journey and outlines future plans during his 50-year entrepreneurial journey. He emphasizes the importance of succession plans and bold investments to ensure growth. Airtel aims to expand into financial services and improve digital infrastructure while keeping cash flow strong. The competitive landscape in telecom presents both challenges and opportunities that Mittal acknowledges.
Sunil Mittal looks beyond telecom as Bharti enters its next chapter
Sunil Mittal wants Bharti Group executives to keep taking risks and make bold bets. As the Bharti Group founder and chairman marks 50 years of his entrepreneurial journey, Mittal, 69, told Kiran Rathee and Vinay Pandey in an interview that his other two key focus areas are drawing up a succession plan and spending more time with the government and political leadership on public policy. Edited excerpts:
**How would you describe this 50-year journey?**
It's been a remarkable journey with the classic ups and downs. But I think the industry that I chose, eventually, from 1992 onwards, the mobile industry, it was quite a different one and a strange sort of story. It's not happened in many countries like this. The policy shifts, the regulatory curveballs, and the multiplicity of players that came through, its unheard of anywhere else—12-13 operators in a country is never seen. So, from that point of view, I would say it's a journey that mirrors India's growth if you look up from 1976 onwards. From a licence raj, where one struggled for permits and licences, import was almost impossible, foreign exchange was non-existent to where we are today, in some sense, I would say Bharti's journey has been in lock step with India’s journey.
Airtel has now come to a point where you can call it a very well-established enterprise or an institution, which is meritocracy-led with high-quality professions driving it. Company’s balance sheet is very strong now after becoming precarious in 2016-18, cash flow is strong, debt is almost non-existent. I think next year we'll have zero public debt and only DoT’s spectrum payments and AGR liabilities will remain.
The company now has to start to think about where to apply cash flow. So we have chosen some new events. Capex of Rs 30,000 crore goes into our regular business like more towers, more fibre, more network, more IT. But in addition to that, financial services, sovereign cloud, and AI data centres--these are three big bets that Airtel is making for India. And some of these will be transported to Africa.
**What about international expansion? Will the same verticals follow?**
I think you need to have strength in your home country. Doing something new in a new place is something which I would avoid. We don't have the chops to do stuff that we've not done in our country. And even when we are doing our core business, like when we went to Africa, the first few years, we struggled because the industry was not new but the place was. So imagine a situation where you are completely new to everything, it’s tough. When we talked to British Telecom (BT), it was familiar territory. And so therefore, I would say, there will be international growth. We are one of the fortunate Indian companies to truly be an MNC. We are now in 15 countries in Africa, we have a stake in BT, the national champion of telecom in Britain, we have a stake in Eutelsat, which is a satellite company. We are already one of the few Indian-based MNCs. For us, not to do more internationally will not be appropriate, we have
to do more. Where, when, the opportunity comes, we have to see. We have the jobs, we have the talent, we have the tools, we have the balance sheet now. We are just waiting for the right opportunities. But it will not be like Africa, where we had gone and picked something big, which was a stress on our global side. Now will be doing tuck-ins (acquisitions) of a few billion here and there. There are opportunities we should keep on looking at but we have to be value seekers, it must come with a good value. Growth is limited in global markets in telecom, so there must be cost takeout opportunities and it must add a significant amount of revenue and ebitda.
**Also Read** | Airtel Money makes London debut after raising $703 million in biggest IPO of the year
**What about succession plans?**
Until a few years back, that was not our priority as we were fighting difficult battles. The question is timely now and I am also working on this. There are two aspects to it. One is Airtel and its ecosystem. That part, I think, succession is already in place with very fine minds and talent who are there. Gopal (Vittal) is lifting himself to a group level, being the executive vice chair with Shashwat (Sharma) taking over in India and Sunil Taldar in Africa. Now the question, therefore, moves to what happens between the shareholder and the professional management. I can answer it at two levels. One is you look at companies like Unilever, where I have been on the board. There is no order. It's run by its people.
British Telecom until we arrived, there was no owner, it was a public company. I had been on the Standard Chartered board, again there was no owner. And then you have Softbank, with Masayoshi Son as a big personality who drives everything. So, I've seen all the models. I think as far as Airtel is concerned, to a large extent, the Unilever model can prevail. So if the family was not to be a shareholder, I think Airtel will be okay with a strong board and running itself. But I'm also conscious that such companies become very risk averse. New bets become very difficult. When things are okay, it works very well. But in a moment of huge crisis, a stewardship or anchor shareholders are required, especially for countries like India and the developing world.
I think my next generation, my sons, my daughter, nephews, they all are coming up into good shape. Both my boys have had years of experience outside, building their own companies, their own ventures, their own fronts. And they are now engaging at the shareholder level. They're getting to see what's going on in Airtel in a much more detailed manner, which was never the case before. So I would say in four or five years, you will start to see step by step those changes happening. Sharvin is already co-chair of Airtel Africa. Gopal is now the chair, I've come off it now. So that’s the first change if you see from the family side, I'm off, he's in.I'm still available for any consultation that Africa or anybody needs. I will still look at the quarterly results, but it's really his job. He's also on the board of Airtel Money. He's been there from day one. And he's looking at many of our international areas of work like satellites and he also has his own fund. And I can see in him a very solid, strong, stable hand who can really deal with very critical aspects of the enterprise.
Kavin is a technologist, but he is also very fine in how companies run. He has run his own company with 250 people, and became a unicorn. He has his own skills, but his focus is deep tech and solving critical and complex issues. He's also got very broad shoulders to deal with a lot of issues. How they combine between themselves has to be worked out as we go forward. My daughter runs a hospitality business with her husband, they are already very successful. They have over 200 hotels globally, managing multiple brands in hospitality. And then, nephews are now coming in--Zubin, Rajan's son, is already in Airtel Finance. He is helping me with Haier, our new investment in consumer appliances. They will develop their own businesses, get their own training in a different way. Rakesh’s son is running his food business. So, we are not the classic family business type of people, we are different. My own view is, treat us as a family in business, not a family business. We are not doctors, lawyers, we are a family in business but we are not a family business. And I think it's a model to be cherished.
**Has the thought crossed your mind that succession can be disruptive as stakeholders increase?**
To my mind, it is a function of any founder that you must leave behind as much clarity as possible. So to your point, yes, it's been on my mind. We have created or laid early foundations of what I call House of Bharti. It's a charter that I have created for the next generation but they are co-creating it with me--how they will deal with issues when things come up, how will they decide if they have disagreements. Those things are now being worked upon but one thing I'm ensuring is in all situations, you bulletproof your enterprises. If there's a contest between the family and enterprise, enterprise wins every time, that's how I see it.
**What about you personally? What is it that you want to do now?**
I think I'd like to see Airtel get to be the first company worldwide with a billion customers. We are 600 million, so we have to get another 400 million. I think India will give us another 200 million, Africa will give us another 100-150 million. So we are still short of 100-150 or 200 million customers. My desire will be to look into markets which have higher ARPUs, higher margins and therefore, we keep spotting opportunities. Those have to be inorganically strapped on. And we'll hopefully get there. Earlier, we were in Bangladesh, which could have given us 20-25 million customers but we have reduced the stake there. We would like to probably exit at some point. Sri Lanka is the same, it’s much smaller. So we have to look at some opportunities. I think the new bets are where I want to spend some time--AI data centre, sovereign cloud, space telecom, how the space will shape up. These are the areas which are taking most of my time.
So if you put this into three parts--one is for the enterprise, how to grow it into new bets, ensure that our professionals keep taking risks, new bold bets. Second is the transition succession plan and the third is how I can personally spend more time with the government and political leadership in public policy.
**Can the tariffs stay low going forward or there should be hikes?**
I would say if you need the nation to have a robust digital spine, you need it to be very healthy. You don't want a situation where you're struggling. And I can tell you today, some of the European markets are struggling. They are behind in the digital journey despite being very rich economies. The US is not, China is not, India is not. And paradoxically, the US is $50-60 ARPU, we have only $3 or less here and we were still able to build it. It's very important that the companies remain very healthy.
While people look at the ebitda margins, it's a wrong metric for telecom companies because a large part of our ebitda that comes through, we spend every year on new capex. There are spectrum auctions that take tens of thousands of crores. It's a very capital-intensive industry. I would say we should build 4x or 5x of what we are today. We should build a million base stations, we are merely 350,000. It’s a long journey, we must have space connectivity, we must have submarine cable, so that in tomorrow's new world, where technology is most important, our fundamental connectivity bedrock is very strong. To that extent, do you need another dollar, dollar and a half--yes. If India gets to Rs 350 ARPU, my stated objective, we will still be lowest in the world. People who can pay a few hundred rupees as tip for opening the car door in a hotel, why can’t they spend Rs 600-700 a month on their phone. It is not a problem for them, but we have artificially kept it so low.
**So there is room for differential pricing?**
Absolutely there is. The unlimited offering at Rs 399 makes no sense at all. Those people will pay a thousand rupees, they'll be comfortable paying a thousand rupees. And then you can actually keep subsidies down for the lower end. By bringing the whole table down, you put some load on the lower end.
**What is stopping companies from offering such tariffs?**
It’s the competition. We have tried to move it, but when the competition doesn't move, you're in the market, you have to be competitive.
We already have a 15-20% premium in tariffs. But that’s the limit.
**There is a lot of noise around the current business environment in India, the rupee, capital outflows. How do you see the situation and what kind of reforms would you expect going ahead?**
I take you back to 1992, when the first wave of reforms happened and that to my mind, should give us a lot of comfort that reforms finally work, and they don't work for just business people, they work for their entire country. I witnessed that from very close quarters. I was a struggling young entrepreneur at that time and that released so much energy in me personally, our enterprise and our people. As a small example, I can tell you, the time you used to spend in the corridors of government, it was gone. The import restrictions were gone, the simplification happened in the custom tariffs and FDI started to open up. That model needs to keep on repeating itself every now and then. I would say we have seen this government very focussed on reforms, and they have done many reforms. And in my own industry, the digital pillar of Prime Minister Modi, from day one, became a very important gain for my industry. He was focussed on ensuring that this digital pillar becomes one of the important pillars of the economy going forward. And that's why you've seen so much growth in our space. Startups, IT industries, the telecom industry, and infrastructure around it. So if I have to give one message back to the government, keep on working on your mantra of ease of doing business--more needs to be done. Sometimes I feel that our political leadership has a bigger ambition, which gets diluted as it starts to get implemented, because every reform that comes has one or two things around it, which lowers the impact of reform. But I think the government is aware. Right now if you see, the government saw the difficulty of price increase, the geopolitical conflicts, the difficulty in supply chain with America becoming insular, trade deals getting into difficulty, China issue and all that. They have moved very quickly to get more dollars into the country. The rupee is below 94 today, a miracle I would say. There were predictions of the rupee going to 100 against the dollar but going back from 97-98 is a miracle. The government is very focussed and conscious and when they see the stock market suffering, capital flows going out, you suddenly see a debate starting--should we look at long-term capital gains in the stock market, should we look at other reforms coming through? My own view is that the next budget that is going to come through may surprise the country, the industry, and many verticals with a lot more ease of doing business coming through. So I would say only one message--keep working more, hear the voice of industry, get more focus groups, invite the industry chambers and firms to talk to you and listen to the needs of the industry. And whichever industry you feel is making supreme profits, then there are ways to tackle that but worry about making the job easier for the industry to do more. And I can tell you, the factories, industries, corporations start to make more money, it goes back into more investment because they're so excited about the opportunities. They invest more money. What's my job every day when our cash flows are going up? I'm not focussed on how much dividends to go out. All the time the conversation is more investments, more investments.
**India now has two $100 billion telcos and financial stress in the sector. Does it open doors for a new entrant like Starlink, which may have ambitions to become a full-fledged telecom player?**
Satcom connectivity is definitely coming, but I strongly believe it's a complementary service and not a supplementary service. It cannot supplement terrestrial networks by its very nature of design. I must compliment Elon Musk that he is pushing the boundaries. The amount of capacity being created was earlier thought to be impossible. So you have to give him the credit but at the same time, the cost for a bit, cost for a GB, is never going to be at a point where he can contest fibre or terrestrial radio connectivity. The US, some markets in Europe, Japan, maybe there is a market to be picked up by satellite because when you have $50-60 ARPU, then there's a game to be played there. You can connect a home and get $50, you can be fine. You can get a mobile customer at $50, you can play the part. But if you see Elon Musk with all his fanciful technology, is picking up local spectrum, is building local networks on the ground and then will combine both. So in the end, even he's saying the same thing that we are saying, you can only be complementary. India has two benefits. One is we are down to $3 ARPU, why would you want to fight a $3 ARPU market, it needs a very high ARPU. Secondly, in India, unlike even the US, we don't have dark spots. We have coverage available everywhere the population is there. It’s unique that in $3 you have covered the entire country. Anywhere in the country, you will get a radio signal, you may not get fibre, which is getting better but you get a 5G radio signal, which is better than a satellite connection. I would say there will be some places, a farmhouse, or oil rig, or something, or a flight connectivity where you will use Starlink or satellite connectivity but on the ground in India, parts of Africa, where we operate, I think the ARPUs are so low, and connectivity is very good, so I don't see a problem. My own view is you will see them combining with local terrestrial operators in India and try their luck in the US.
**Amid the discussions over currency, there's been talk that we need to look at outbound investment. What are your thoughts on that?**
I think this is an interesting question. We have almost always been encouraged to go and spread India to the world. That took us to Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the UK and Europe. So we have always been encouraged at every level in the government. It's a matter of pride for a few Indian companies to go out into the world, taking Indian talent, taking technology, and Indian ways of working. In the end, this wealth that is sitting outside, where does it sit? It belongs to India. So you have these dollars, pound revenues coming through--they all belong to India. Unlike some of my peers who switched overseas and invested from outside of India, we invest from India outside, so entire Africa, Africa Money, British Telecom, Eutelsat are owned from India. They are governed by Indian regulations, RBI, my investments are all from India. So they're all Indian assets. I would never compromise what is needed to invest in India at the cost of going out. But when you have exhausted your opportunities here, India is actually beckoning a handful of companies to go out. It builds our soft power, it builds our diplomatic relationships. It builds our presence in those countries, even politically.
**Jio has listed and India already has a kind of duopoly. How do you see the domestic market?**
It is good that the listing has happened, which is an important event for a large company like Jio. We have four companies, out of which two are fully and partly owned by the government. There is some cooperation between Vodafone Idea and BSNL. So I would say in that sense, there are three companies--it's a perfect size, perfect market dynamics. We need to be freshly healthy. When there were 12 operators, everybody was suboptimal, spectrum was fragmented, we were struggling
to provide quality. Nobody was investing money, they were just doing cities and trying to compete in the key economic markets, ignoring the rural areas. So I would say this is a perfect combination. China has three, the UK has moved on to three, the US has had three for long, and in Africa, most of them are two operators. So I would say in India, it is ideal to have three operators. They must be encouraged, they must be tasked to build more and more in the coming years.

New Delhi: 

From a Rs 45-crore 4-BHK to a Rs 271-crore penthouse, DLF is building a luxury housing ladder in Gurugram.

The recent Rs 271-crore purchase at DLF's The Dahlias by entrepreneur Manav Sardana has put the spotlight on the developer's super-luxury homes once again. But The Dahlias is only the latest stop in DLF's high-end residential journey.

The story stretches from The Magnolias to The Camellias and now The Dahlias.

At The Magnolias, a 4-BHK home starts at around Rs 45 crore. The size is about 6,400 sq ft.

The project is part of DLF's super-luxury residential portfolio and has also attracted well-known names. Cricket legend Kapil Dev is among those associated with The Magnolias.

The amenities include a lawn terrace, clubhouse, gym, kids' play area, swimming pool, jogging track, skating rink, multipurpose lawn and surface car parks.

For buyers at this level, the home is only part of the package. The wider development, facilities and privacy are part of what they are paying for.

## Then Comes The Camellias

DLF's The Camellias takes the luxury pitch several notches higher.

DLF describes The Camellias as its most luxurious residential offering in its super-luxury portfolio. The project combines high-end architecture, landscaped spaces, views, amenities and personalised services.

But its biggest talking point may be the people who have bought homes there. The list includes some of India's best-known business and startup names.

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal bought a super-luxury apartment for Rs 52.3 crore.

Berkshire Hathaway vice chairman Ajit Jain bought a roughly 7,400 sq ft apartment for around Rs 85 crore. Smiti Agarwal, the wife of Hemant Agarwal, CMD of retail giant V-Bazaar, bought a luxury apartment for Rs 95 crore, while British entrepreneur Sukhpal Singh Ahluwalia bought an apartment for around Rs 100 crore.

Then there is entrepreneur Rishi Parti. He bought a 16,290 sq ft penthouse at The Camellias for Rs 190 crore.

The Camellias has also been associated with several familiar names from India's startup world, including Aman Gupta of boAt, Peyush Bansal of Lenskart, Ashneer Grover, Vikram Chopra of Cars24, Varun Alagh of Mamaearth, Lokvir Kapoor of Pine Labs and Good Earth founder Anita Lal.

## And The Dahlias

A 4 BHK at The Dahlias starts at around Rs 65 crore. The size is about 9,500 sq ft. But the Rs 65-crore starting price is only the beginning.

The project has already seen several transactions running into hundreds of crores.

Another Delhi-NCR-based industrialist (name not disclosed) bought four interconnected apartments for Rs 380 crore. The homes together span more than 35,000 sq ft.

Investor Madhusudan Murlidhar Kela bought a luxury apartment for Rs 120.71 crore, according to the buyer information shared with NDTV. And then came Manav Sardana's Rs 271-crore penthouse purchase.

The penthouse has a 17,200 sq ft super area and 10,500 sq ft carpet area. At around Rs 1.58 lakh per sq ft on super area, the deal works out to nearly Rs 2.6 lakh per sq ft on carpet area.

The transaction is among the biggest single-unit residential deals reported in India.

The project offers facilities such as a gym, swimming pool, meditation centre, jogging track, garden and 24x7 security.

## Address Is The Biggest Attraction

The appeal of these projects goes beyond the size of the apartment.

The Magnolias offers everything from a swimming pool and gym to a skating rink, jogging track and clubhouse.

The Dahlias adds facilities such as a meditation centre, swimming pool, gym, jogging track, garden and round-the-clock security. According to DLF, The Dahlias will span around 7.5 million square feet and comprise 420 residences across 29 levels and 8 towers, including 15 exclusive duplex penthouses of about 350,000 square feet.

The Camellias, meanwhile, has been positioned by DLF around architecture, landscaping, views, amenities and personalised services.

But perhaps the biggest attraction is the address itself. Over the years, the DLF Golf Links ecosystem has become associated with some of India's wealthiest business families, entrepreneurs and corporate leaders.

And now, with The Dahlias pushing individual home prices to Rs 271 crore and beyond, the luxury ladder has reached a new level.

# DLF Limited: Crafting empires by transforming urban landscapes

## Chairman Rajiv Singh is charting a future where luxury is not merely lived. He says the company is selling a lifestyle and a legacy with their homes

By Forbes India Last Updated: Oct 08, 2025, 14:44 IST 1 min

Rajiv Singh, Chairman, DLF Limited Image: Caricatures by Kapil Kashyap with the help of Grok.Ai

Rajiv Singh doesn’t just build homes—he crafts empires. As chairman of DLF Limited, India’s largest real estate developer with a market cap of ₹1,88,037.31 crore, Singh has transformed urban landscapes into bastions of luxury. Founded in 1946, DLF pioneered luxury residential development in India, introducing iconic projects like The Magnolias and The Aralias in Gurugram in the early 2000s. These developments, launched in 2004 and 2005 respectively, set enduring standards for opulence with sprawling residences, golf-course views, and exclusive amenities, establishing DLF as the gold standard for India’s affluent. Today, the company delivers sustainable, innovative communities that command premiums 20 to 50 percent above market averages, blending prestige with eco-conscious design.

Born in 1959, Singh is the third-generation torchbearer of DLF, founded by his grandfather Chaudhary Raghvendra Singh and scaled by his father, Kushal Pal Singh. A mechanical engineering graduate from MIT, he brings precision and foresight to an industry often mired in volatility. “Real estate thrives on sustainability, not bubbles,” Singh declared in a 2025 interview, a mantra reflected in DLF’s record-breaking ₹21,700 crore pre-sales in FY25, with a goal of ₹20,000–22,500 crore for FY26. His net worth, exceeding $14.4 billion, cements his status as India’s richest real estate magnate, with a FY25 compensation of ₹37 crore.

DLF targets the uber-luxury segment—properties above ₹20 crore—where scarcity drives value. Its flagship, The Camellias in Gurugram, spans 17.5 acres with 429 ultra-large residences starting at ₹7.8 million. Facing a golf course, these homes offer private elevators, wellness hubs, and LEED-certified designs, appealing to eco-conscious buyers. DLF’s formula—exclusive locations, bespoke amenities and smart technology—yields stellar return on investment, and high rental returns in a low-inventory market. “We’re selling a lifestyle, a legacy,” Singh told shareholders in 2025.

The Camellias has become a beacon for India’s business elite, drawing visionaries like Zomato’s Deepinder Goyal, who purchased a 10,813 sq ft residence for ₹52 crore in 2025, and Lenskart’s Peyush Bansal, both Shark Tank stars.

In 2024, DLF deepened its NCR footprint. Its Gurugram launch ‘Privana South’ saw bookings of ₹7,200 crore within days, and together with other FY24-FY25 Gurugram launches, cumulative bookings are expected to surpass ₹10,000 crore.

Singh is charting a future where luxury is not merely lived—it’s timeless. His leadership ensures DLF remains the pinnacle of India’s aspirational lifestyle.

## M3M Sector 113 Projects: Complete Pricing, Floor Plans & Launch Status in 2026

M3M has emerged as one of Gurgaon's most aggressive developers on the Dwarka Expressway, with multiple distinct residential projects now in various stages of launch and construction across Sector 113. The corridor has become the focal point of NCR's real estate conversation, but the sheer number of M3M developments in this single sector—each with different specifications, pricing, and possession timelines—has created widespread confusion among homebuyers. This guide separates the projects and clarifies what's available, what it costs, and what buyers should verify before committing.

## The M3M Portfolio in Sector 113: Which Projects Are Live?

M3M operates at least three to four distinct residential projects within Sector 113, each occupying different parcels and catering to different buyer segments. The most visible are M3M Capital (including its multiple phases), M3M Mansion, and M3M Smart City (also marketed as M3M Golf Estate or variations). Each has its own RERA registration, pricing, floor plans, and possession date. This fragmentation is deliberate—M3M is using multiple brands and positioning to target different wealth segments.

M3M Capital Sector 113 is the flagship ultra-luxury residential development directly on the Dwarka Expressway. This is a high-rise, high-density project split into two phases, with Phase 1 comprising 2.5 BHK, 3.5 BHK, and 4.5 BHK configurations ranging from 1,310 to 2,249 sq. ft. The project was registered with HRERA under number GGM/531/263/2022/06 on February 2, 2022, for Phase 1, and subsequently registered for Phase 2 under GGM/612/344/2022/87.

M3M Mansion Sector 113 is a separate ultra-luxury offering marketed with an even more premium positioning, featuring larger 4 BHK and 5 BHK penthouses on approximately 10 acres. Mansion is registered under HARERA/GGM/802/534/2024/29 with a much later possession date of February 2032, making it a longer hold for investors.

M3M Smart City (SCDA) is the integrated 65-acre township concept within the larger Smart City Delhi Airport (SCDA) development, marketed with golf-themed amenities and resort-style living. This comprises portions of Capital and potentially separate branded verticals aimed at the ultra-HNI segment.

## Pricing Across M3M Sector 113 Projects: Why Quotes Vary So Widely

One critical issue buyers face immediately: no two sources quote the same price for M3M Sector 113. Industry analysis reveals genuine price ranges of ₹2.93 crore to ₹6.19 crore for what appears to be similar 3.5 BHK units, alongside vastly different per-sq.-ft. rates ranging from ₹15,750 to ₹20,000+. This is not a data error—it reflects legitimate variability driven by phase, floor level, orientation, configuration variation, and the date of the quote.

M3M Capital Phase 1 indicative pricing: 2 BHK (1,310 sq. ft.) starting from ₹2.4 crore onwards; 3 BHK (1,665 sq. ft.) from ₹3.3 crore; 4 BHK (2,298 sq. ft.) from ₹4.4 crore. Some channel partners cite starting prices of ₹1.3 crore for 2 BHK and ₹1.8 crore for 3 BHK, but these appear to reflect either older pre-launch quotes or extended subvention plans that defer a portion of cost.

M3M Mansion pricing: Significantly higher—3.5 BHK starting from ₹3.5 crore to ₹4.5 crore; 4.5 BHK and larger penthouses from ₹5 crore to ₹14.73 crore for premium configurations. Average capital cost runs to approximately ₹18,000 per sq. ft. compared to ₹16,000 for standard Sector 113 benchmarks, reflecting Mansion's ultra-premium positioning.

M3M Capital price per sq. ft.: Based on current quotes, approximately ₹18,000–₹20,000 per sq. ft. on a built-up basis. This places the project at the upper range of Dwarka Expressway pricing, well above mass-luxury projects but below ultra-trophy properties on Golf Course Road.

## Floor Plans & Unit Mix: What Configurations Are Available?

M3M Capital dominates the current launch activity in Sector 113 with a broad range of unit types to capture different buyer segments within the ultra-luxury bracket:

- 2.5 BHK: 1,310 sq. ft., designed as a "luxury 2-BHK+." Carpeted layouts are tight compared to traditional 2-BHKs, but the ultra-luxury branding justifies premium pricing. Aimed at empty nesters, international expats, and investors seeking liquid units.
- 3.5 BHK: 1,665 sq. ft., the "sweet spot" in the project. Floor plans emphasize open living, large balconies with city or green views, and a segregated servants' area. Most repeat buyers from M3M's previous launches opt for this configuration.
- 4 & 4.5 BHK: 2,055–2,298 sq. ft. Includes dedicated lounges, multiple ensuites, and extensive balconies. These appeal to NRI families and Delhi-based executives seeking a second home with premium specifications.

Key floor plan principles: Most units are designed with three sides open to maximize natural light and cross-ventilation. This differentiates M3M Capital from competitors where high-rise density often results in units with two-sided or compromised exposures. Vaastu-compliant layouts are standard across configurations. Two-level parking is included—a standard amenity for the price point.

## Possession Dates & Construction Status: Timelines You Must Verify

This is where precision becomes critical because conflicting timelines circulate across sources. As of September 2026:

- M3M Capital Phase 1: Originally promised for June 2026; current developer communications cite December 2026 as revised expected completion. This is a 6-month slip from the original RERA disclosure. Buyers who locked in early may have different possession expectations than recent buyers.
- M3M Capital Phase 2: Typically scheduled 12–18 months after Phase 1, suggesting late 2027 or early 2028 for possession.
- M3M Mansion: February 2032—a full 5–6 year hold from current booking date. This is not a near-term possession project and should only appeal to investors with deep pockets and long time horizons.

Always verify the specific possession timeline for the phase, tower, and floor you are considering. RERA registration documents and site visit confirmations from the developer sales team are the only reliable sources; aggregator websites often lag behind updated timelines by 6+ months.

## Payment Plans & Booking Terms: How Much Cash Do You Need Upfront?

M3M offers multiple payment structures to reduce upfront burden and attract different buyer profiles:

- 10:90 Subvention Plan: Only 10% of the total value due at booking, with 90% financed through construction and payable at possession or over a staggered timeline. This dramatically reduces initial capital requirement but ties cash for the full project duration.
- 30:70 Plan: 30% within 3 months of launch; remaining 70% at possession. A middle-ground approach favored by mid-term investors.
- 30:30:40 or similar variants: 30% on booking, 30% on completion of superstructure, 40% on OC application or possession.
- Assured Return Options: Select units come with 7% assured returns on 50% payment until OC is applied—a feature marketed to NRI investors seeking stable yields during construction.

Booking amount (typically 10–20% of the unit price) must be paid at the time of signing the purchase agreement. Then payments are phased across milestones. Do not commit without reviewing the actual payment schedule linked to the unit and tower you intend to purchase; timelines differ significantly between phases.

## Amenities: Golf Course, Clubhouse & Community Facilities

M3M's positioning hinges heavily on lifestyle amenities. M3M Capital boasts one of the largest clubhouses on Dwarka Expressway, spanning 60,000–75,000 sq. ft. across 4 levels with 50+ curated amenities. Flagship offerings include:

- 9-hole professional golf course and putting greens (golf-themed landscaping extends across central courtyards)
- Olympic-sized swimming pool with heated water option
- State-of-the-art gymnasium with personal training studios
- Spa and wellness center
- Indoor sports: badminton courts, squash, table tennis, billiards
- Outdoor jogging/cycling track and yoga areas
- Amphitheatre for community events
- Multiple dining outlets including lounge, cafe, and themed restaurant
- Kids' play areas and teens' gaming zone

Over 70% of the total project area is dedicated to open, landscaped green spaces. This low-density positioning—despite high-rise towers of 18–36 floors—differentiates M3M Capital from competing ultra-luxury projects in the corridor that prioritize higher FSI efficiency.

## Location & Connectivity: The "Zero KM from Delhi" Advantage

M3M Capital sits directly on the Dwarka Expressway at the literal Delhi-Gurgaon border. This unique positioning creates what market analysts term the "Arbitrage of Geography"—buyers pay Gurgaon prices but gain Delhi connectivity with none of the congestion.

Key commute profiles:

- Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI): 10 minutes by car via expressway
- Dwarka Sector 25 Metro Station: 3 km (approximately 8–10 minutes depending on internal road completion)
- Diplomatic Enclave & South Delhi: 15–20 minutes
- Cyber City & MG Road, Gurgaon: 12–15 minutes
- Golf Course Road, Gurgaon: 15–18 minutes
- Gurugram CBD and Udyog Vihar: 20–25 minutes

This makes M3M Capital highly attractive to NRI expats, diplomats, and Delhi-based executives who work in or travel frequently via IGI Airport. Rental demand is correspondingly high from this cohort.

Infrastructure note: While the main Dwarka Expressway is fully functional, internal sector roads within Sectors 108–113 remain partially unpaved or under development. This last-mile connectivity gap is a real concern for daily commute convenience, though unlikely to impact long-term appreciation once internal roads complete (likely 2027–2028 timelines).

## RERA Status & Regulatory Compliance

M3M Capital is RERA-registered under multiple approved numbers reflecting different phases and parcels:

- Phase 1: GGM/531/263/2022/06, registered February 2, 2022
- Phase 2: GGM/612/344/2022/87, registered September 28, 2022

Project details, including updated possession dates, payment schedules, and material breach clauses, are available on the HRERA (Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority) portal at hrera.nic.in. Buyers should cross-check any verbal commitments against the official RERA document before proceeding.

M3M India has completed 62+ residential projects across Gurgaon over 12+ years. Track record for timely delivery is strong relative to the broader developer cohort, though recent Phase 1 timeline slip from June to December 2026 suggests execution headwinds are real.

## Buyer Sentiment & Reviews: What Are Actual Buyers Saying?

Reviews for M3M Capital are mixed and reflect the tension between aspirational marketing and ground-reality concerns:

Positive feedback: Location is repeatedly praised as unbeatable—zero-km-from-Delhi advantage, expressway access, and IGI Airport proximity are genuine. The golf-themed design and extensive clubhouse differentiate the project from competitor high-rises. Investors appreciate the strong rental potential from the expat and diplomat community. Developer credibility (M3M's 62+ completed projects) provides assurance relative to new-entrant builders.

Concerns raised: Pricing is consistently flagged as on the higher side compared to adjacent ultra-luxury options. Several buyers note the project feels overvalued relative to similar unit sizes and amenities at competing locations like Golf Course Road or South Delhi proximity (which commands similar pricing). Possession delays—the June 2026 slip to December—have eroded confidence among early-stage investors expecting liquidity. Internal road completion remains unclear; buyers purchasing for immediate occupancy should physically verify last-mile connectivity before booking. Long possession timelines (December 2026 for Phase 1, 2027–2028 for Phase 2) tie capital for 18–24+ months, a consideration for buyers with liquidity needs.

Overall rating across aggregator platforms: 4.0/5 to 4.2/5, reflecting solid confidence in M3M's brand but genuine reservations about valuation and timing.

## Investment Outlook & Capital Appreciation Potential

Market analysts estimate forward appreciation in the Dwarka Expressway corridor at 8–15% per annum for premium-segment properties, a significant slowdown from the 40–50%+ appreciation seen in 2020–2023. The explosive growth phase of this corridor is considered largely complete.

Key appreciation drivers going forward:

- Metro extension confirmation: The Blue Line extension from Dwarka towards sectors 102–113 is confirmed for 2026–27 opening. However, the strongest price impact is projected for Sectors 102–109; Sector 113 is somewhat peripheral to this node.
- Commercial hub maturation: The International Convention Centre (Yashobhoomi) and Diplomatic Enclave II nearby are anchoring high-end commercial and hospitality use, which typically supports residential value.
- NRI rental demand: As the expat community expands within Delhi NCR, Sector 113's positioning as a premium, secure, serviced-apartment-like environment will continue attracting institutional and individual investor interest.

Realistic buyer perspective: M3M Capital should be viewed as a 5–7 year hold for meaningful capital gain (double-digit returns), not a 2–3 year flip. The current pricing has already priced in "location premium" and some infrastructure excitement; upside is moderate, not explosive.

## Should You Book M3M Capital Now? A Buyer Checklist

Book now if: You are a Delhi-based or NRI professional with 24+ month investment horizon; you work near IGI Airport or Diplomatic Enclave and value actual commute time over paper appreciation; you can afford the 10–30% upfront booking amount without strain; you appreciate luxury amenities and don't mind paying 10–15% premium for design and lifestyle differentiation.

Wait or look elsewhere if: You need possession within 12 months; you expect rapid 30–40% appreciation (unrealistic in current market); you are price-sensitive and view ultra-luxury amenities as secondary; you are concerned about last-mile connectivity and want a ready-to-move address; you cannot afford the ₹2.4+ crore minimum entry price and are seeking value-for-money ultra-luxury.

Critical due diligence steps: Visit the site during peak traffic hours to verify actual commute times to your workplace or the airport. Request recent RERA-registered payment schedules and confirmation of revised possession dates directly from M3M sales team—do not rely on old brochures. Cross-check pricing by comparing identical floor plans across multiple phases; price per sq. ft. should be relatively stable within a phase. Request references from 3–4 buyers from M3M's previous Gurgaon projects to assess post-occupancy service and delivery realism. Hire a property lawyer to review the purchase agreement and payment milestones before signing.

If M3M Capital's pricing feels steep, comparable ultra-luxury options on Dwarka Expressway include Smartworld Forest Estate (nearby Sector 112–113), Prestige Group's Dwarka Expressway projects in adjacent sectors, and select phases of Godrej's properties in the corridor. All offer similar connectivity but often at ₹15,000–₹17,000 per sq. ft. compared to M3M's ₹18,000–₹20,000. None, however, replicate M3M's scale of amenities or green-space dedication.

## Final Verdict

M3M Capital Sector 113 is a legitimate ultra-luxury address with genuine location strengths, strong developer credentials, and differentiated lifestyle positioning. It is not a speculative bet—it is a long-term core holding for buyers who prioritize actual commute convenience and premium living standards over rapid appreciation. Current pricing is fair given location, but not cheap; buyers should negotiate hard on launch discounts and payment plan flexibility rather than expect significant price movement post-booking.

## The Legacy Question: Why It Actually Matters for Resale

DLF didn't just build in Gurgaon — DLF largely created the version of Gurgaon that exists today. Cyber City, CyberHub, and Golf Course Road are DLF developments that turned a sleepy district into India's corporate capital. That matters practically: when a DLF project comes up for resale, the buyer pool already trusts the address before they've seen the apartment. That trust shortens negotiation cycles and supports price floors during market dips — something brokers will quietly tell you matters more than people realize until they're the one trying to exit a property in a slow quarter.

M3M is a much younger company — incorporated in 2010 — but it scaled unusually fast by going aggressive on design and amenities rather than waiting decades to build reputation organically. The tradeoff: M3M's resale market is thinner simply because most of its inventory hasn't gone through a full ownership cycle yet. That's not necessarily a red flag — it's a function of age, not quality — but it does mean liquidity-sensitive buyers should factor in longer expected holding periods.

### Location Strategy: Proven Ground vs. Growth Bets

This is where the comparison actually gets useful, because the two builders have deliberately chosen different sides of the risk-reward curve.

DLF has anchored itself in markets that are already "made." Golf Course Road, established sectors of Gurgaon, and proximity to Cyber City mean DLF buyers are paying for certainty — existing social infrastructure, proven schools and hospitals nearby, and metro/NH-8 connectivity that's already functional, not promised.

M3M has bet on corridors that are still being built out. Golf Course Extension Road was a relatively quiet stretch before M3M Golf Estate anchored it; the same playbook is now running on Dwarka Expressway with projects like M3M Crown and M3M Capital. The logic here is straightforward infrastructure economics: Dwarka Expressway connects Gurgaon directly to Delhi, IGI Airport, and Aerocity, and large parts of that road network have come online only in the last 2–3 years. Early movers in any Gurgaon corridor historically capture more appreciation than those who buy after the corridor is "obviously" desirable — but the flip side is that timeline delays in supporting infrastructure (roads, metro extensions) directly affect your holding period.

If you're choosing based on location alone: DLF if you want a known quantity today, M3M if you're underwriting the next 5-year growth story and can tolerate some infrastructure-timeline risk.

### Pricing, ROI, and What the Numbers Actually Suggest

This is the section most comparisons skip entirely, and it's the one that matters most to an investor.

DLF's ultra-luxury launches — The Camellias, Privana North, The Dahlias — have consistently commanded premium per-sq-ft rates and sold out within days of launch, with reported bookings running into thousands of crores. That kind of absorption speed tells you two things: there's deep NRI and HNI demand for the DLF brand, and resale exits in these projects tend to be faster than the broader market.

M3M's pricing sits across a wider band. Flagship luxury products can approach DLF-level pricing, but a large share of M3M's portfolio — particularly along Dwarka Expressway and in Manesar — is positioned at meaningfully lower entry points. For an investor, that's the actual thesis: lower entry cost plus a corridor that's still maturing equals higher theoretical appreciation room than buying into an already-peaked micro-market.

A practical caveat worth being direct about: "higher appreciation potential" is a forward-looking claim, not a guarantee. It depends on infrastructure delivery timelines (NPR, Dwarka Expressway completion stretches, metro connectivity) actually holding. Treat any specific CAGR number you see quoted online — including ones that sound precise — with skepticism unless it's sourced to a dated, named report. The honest version of this comparison is: DLF = lower risk, lower but more certain returns. M3M (especially Dwarka Expressway assets) = higher potential upside, tied to infrastructure execution risk.

Disclaimer: Pricing and appreciation figures referenced here are indicative and change frequently. Always verify current rates directly with the developer's sales office and cross-check against recent registered transaction data before making a financial decision. This is not investment advice.

### Project Face-Off: How This Plays Out in Real Decisions

Brand-level comparisons are useful but buyers usually end up choosing between two specific projects. Two recurring face-offs:

M3M Golf Estate vs. DLF The Camellias — Both anchor their respective corridors, but they're not really direct competitors on price. The Camellias sits at the very top of Gurgaon's luxury ladder; M3M Golf Estate is positioned a tier below on price but competes hard on amenity density (56-acre golf-themed layout, resort-style clubhouse). Buyers comparing these two are usually choosing between "absolute prestige" and "amenity value for money."

M3M Crown vs. DLF Privana North — This is the more relevant face-off for mid-to-upper luxury buyers. Privana North benefits from DLF's brand pull and sold out at launch; M3M Crown competes on Dwarka Expressway positioning and a lower per-sq-ft entry point. If your decision criteria is "fastest probable resale," Privana North currently has the edge. If it's "lowest entry cost into a corridor with infrastructure tailwinds," M3M Crown is the stronger argument.

## Governance, RERA, and the Due-Diligence Step Nobody Skips (But Should Do First)

DLF is India's largest listed real estate company, which means it operates under continuous public disclosure requirements — audited financials, shareholder reporting, the works. For risk-averse and institutional-adjacent buyers (and especially NRIs who can't easily monitor a project in person), that transparency is a real advantage.

M3M is privately held. That doesn't automatically mean higher risk, but it does mean the burden of verification shifts more to the buyer. Before booking anything — with M3M or any privately held developer — pull the project's RERA registration number directly from the Haryana RERA portal, check the registered completion date against the developer's marketed completion date, and look at the construction-linked plan (CLP) milestones versus actual construction progress photos if available. This single step — comparing RERA-declared timelines against ground reality — is the difference between buyers who get blindsided by delays and buyers who don't.

One practical broker-side observation: CLP (construction-linked plan) payment structures protect the buyer better than down-payment (DP) plans, because your money releases in step with verified construction milestones rather than upfront. If a project is being aggressively pushed on a DP plan with a discount attached, that discount is the developer pricing in their own need for early liquidity — worth noting, not necessarily a dealbreaker, but worth noting.

### Lifestyle and Buyer Perception

Perception differences are real and they show up in resale conversations, not just brochures.

DLF reads as the "blue-chip" choice — understated design, generational-wealth positioning, the kind of address that doesn't need explaining to an older buyer or an NRI parent. M3M reads as the contemporary, amenity-forward choice — infinity pools, themed clubhouses, smart-home features — and tends to resonate more with younger HNI buyers and first-time luxury upgraders who want a project that photographs and lives like a five-star resort.

Neither perception is "wrong." It's a fit question: who is going to actually live there, and what do they value day to day versus what they'll explain to a future buyer.

- Risk-averse, capital-preservation focused, possibly NRI: DLF. Established micro-market, listed-company transparency, faster resale exits.
- Growth-oriented investor with a 5–7 year horizon, comfortable with corridor risk: M3M, specifically Dwarka Expressway or Golf Course Extension Road assets, with RERA timelines independently verified.

## FAQs

Is M3M as good as DLF?

"As good" depends on what you're optimizing for. DLF has stronger resale liquidity and governance transparency; M3M offers more accessible entry pricing and stronger theoretical appreciation in growth corridors. Neither is objectively better across every metric.

Which is better for investment, DLF or M3M?

For lower-risk, faster-exit investment, DLF's established micro-markets are generally the safer bet. For higher-upside, longer-horizon investment, M3M's Dwarka Expressway and Golf Course Extension Road projects carry more appreciation potential, paired with more infrastructure-timeline risk.

Does DLF have better resale value than M3M?

Generally yes, in established projects, simply because DLF's secondary market is deeper and older. M3M's resale market is thinner mainly because much of its inventory hasn't completed a full ownership cycle yet, not necessarily because of demand weakness.

Is M3M overpriced compared to DLF?

Not typically — M3M's portfolio spans a wider price band, and a large share of its inventory is positioned below DLF's flagship pricing. Flagship-tier M3M products can approach DLF pricing, but the broader portfolio remains more accessible.

What's the rental yield difference between M3M and DLF properties?

Rental yields in both portfolios are driven more by micro-market commercial activity (proximity to Cyber City, NPR, upcoming business districts) than by builder brand alone. Verify current rental rates for the specific sector rather than relying on brand-level assumptions.

## Philosophy

The well-being of all our stakeholders is at the core of our operating philosophy. Our focus on well-being permeates the entire process, from design to execution, and operations, leading to an unparalleled experience.

Guided by our philosophy of Work _Well_ and Live _Well_, we aspire to create differentiated working and living experiences, in the commercial and residential segments, respectively. We ensure this by moving beyond the conventional separation of work, life, and well-being, and paying attention to the entire spectrum of wellness across physical, emotional, social, and environmental aspects.

## Empathetic Hospitality

An intelligent approach to hospitality and service values empathy. We understand the emotional and social needs of our customers, and create spaces where they feel cared for.

## Environmental Harmony

We focus on holistic well-being, with immense attention paid to every element. Focus on elements like air, water and biophilia through interventions that aim to provide fresh air, water, and integrate green designs enable us to build developments that prioritise our users.

## Generosity

We believe in going beyond the required norm, to build generosity of time, space, and attention to detail into our spaces.

## Intentional Design

Our interventions are carefully to promote a healthier lifestyle, with the help of technology and design. We offer comfort with the right ergonomics, and thermal considerations. We integrate aesthetics with functionality, by including carefully curated artwork in our developments and encourage physical movement by building mobility into our spaces.

## Inclusivity

Our spaces are designed for the well-being of all in mind, irrespective of age, gender, ability and circumstances.

## Peace Of Mind

Our endeavor is to enable well-being for our users, in all ways possible. By carefully choosing well connected locations, opting for highest standards of sanitation and, and ensuring safety measures are in place, we build our users’ peace of mind into our developments.

## Belonging

Our developments promote social well-being by integrating amenities and events that promote engagement and interaction, leading to a true sense of community.

## Sustainability

Safeguarding the environment through energy and resource efficiency is the core principle of its sustainable development policy.

## Food and Nurtition

We care for the health and well-being of our customers by offering easy access to organic vegetables and biotic food sales. We also offer curated F&B options with focus on quality & nutrition.

At Max Estates, we believe that spaces should elevate how people live, work, and thrive. Guided by our theme for 2025, “Redefining Spaces, Pioneering Wellbeing,” we are committed to shaping a future where real estate is not defined by square footage but by the quality of life it fosters.

Our approach reimagines real estate as a catalyst for holistic wellness, designing interconnected environments that foster collaboration, innovation, and community. Whether through immersive LiveWell homes or thoughtfully designed WorkWell offices, wellbeing is not an afterthought but the very foundation of our vision.

Rooted in our core values of Sevabhav, Excellence, and Credibility, we strive to create environments where design aligns with intent and growth serves a greater purpose. Our LiveWell, WorkWell philosophy supports intergenerational harmony in homes and enhances commercial spaces for productivity and vitality—truly pioneering a new paradigm of wellbeing in the built environment.

Our developments, from wellness-certified office spaces like Max Square, Max Towers, and Max House to community-focused residential projects such as Estate 128 and Estate 360, demonstrate our commitment to redefining spaces that promote physical, emotional, social, and environmental wellness. In this report, we outline how Max Estates is intentionally and thoughtfully redefining real estate and urban living, focusing on holistic wellbeing and delivering tangible and transformative value.

#### LETTER TO THE SHAREHOLDERS

Dear Shareholders,

It is both an honour and a privilege to present our inaugural Integrated Annual Report as we mark a milestone year of purposeful growth and meaningful expansion. The theme, “Redefining Spaces, Pioneering Wellbeing”, captures the essence of our journey as we step into a new phase shaped by scale, clarity, sustainability, and execution.

FY2025 marks the beginning of Max Estates’ 3.0 execution phase. This was a strategic shift from being a single-project developer to becoming a purpose-driven real estate organisation delivering multiple large-scale projects across Delhi NCR.

This evolution has been grounded in capital discipline, capability enhancement, and an unwavering belief in our vision of bringing real wellbeing into real estate.

Global and Domestic Context: Resilience Amid Uncertainty

The global economic environment in 2024 remained complex and uneven. Several large economies faced long-term challenges. The United States stayed resilient, backed by consumer demand. Europe struggled to regain momentum and China’s real estate sector remained under pressure.

India, in contrast, outperformed global trends. Our economy remained stable with a positive outlook. GDP grew at an estimated 6.5%, making India one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world. Inflation eased, private and public investments picked up pace, and structural reforms continued to advance. Together, these factors strengthened India’s standing as a resilient, reliable growth engine in a challenging global context.

India’s real estate sector reflected this momentum. Institutional investments rose to $8.9 billion, a 51% increase over the previous year. Despite constrained supply, residential sales remained strong. The sector continues to be a key pillar to India’s economic and employment ecosystem.

The residential market saw a clear shift towards premium and luxury homes, driven by rising aspirations, greater affordability, and growing trust in branded developers. Commercial real estate also saw record momentum. India reached its highest-ever gross leasing volume of 79 million square feet, reflecting strong occupier confidence and the country’s rising appeal as a destination for Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

Scaling with Purpose: The Max Estates 3.0 Journey

As the market continues to evolve, we continue to grow with intention. The Max Estates 3.0 journey is grounded in strong fundamentals, including a focus on strategic locations and wellbeing-enabled ecosystems, high-quality design, customer-first experiences, and disciplined use of capital. This approach strengthens our foundation as a forward thinking real estate brand, ready to lead with purpose and clarity.

In line with our approach, FY2025 was a defining year for Max Estates—a year of moving from preparation to execution, from planning to performance, marking milestones across these key pillars.

» Our total portfolio grew from 8 million to over 17.1 million square feet, with a balanced mix of residential, commercial, and mixed-use developments across Noida, Gurugram, and Delhi. We evolved from managing one project to overseeing four operational assets, four under construction, and three in design. We acquired prime land and development rights across Delhi NCR, enhancing our vision to redefine real estate with contemporary design and a hospitality-led experience. This growth was shaped by deliberate strategic choices, rooted in product quality, innovation, and holistic customer experience.

India, in contrast, outperformed global trends. Our economy remained stable with a positive outlook. GDP grew at an estimated 6.5%, making India one of the fastest growing major economies in the world.

Mr. Analjit Singh Founder & Chairman, Max Group

Mr. Sahil Vachani Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Max Estates

We witnessed strong momentum in the residential segment. Pre-sales crossed ₹5,300 crore, a threefold rise from the previous year. Among our residential (LiveWell) offerings, Estate 128 in Noida is now fully sold, with Phase II launched at over 40% premium to Phase I, reaffirming the value of thoughtful design and customer-first experiences in residential communities. Estate 360 in Gurugram, Delhi NCR’s first intergenerational living concept, also saw a strong response. With 96% of its inventory sold, it recorded ₹4,634 crore in sales. Together, collections crossed ₹980 crore. It was a clear reflection of our execution and customer-centric approach.

In the commercial segment, we focused on creating spaces that deliver high-quality, differentiated experiences. Max Square in Noida reached over 99% leasing, at a 30% rental premium to its micro market. Max House Phase II in Delhi reached full occupancy within 12 months, at a 60% premium. Our commercial portfolio now spans over 6 million square feet across delivered, ongoing, and upcoming developments. Together, they carry a peak annuity rental potential of ₹720 crore. Each of our commercial assets is fully leased and home to a diverse mix of tenants. No single occupier holds more than 25% of space in any development, reaffirming that our leasing model remains resilient and built to last.

Capital Strength and Strategic Partnerships

FY2025 was also a year of strengthening our capital base. We raised over ₹1,300 crore of fresh capital through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), strategic investor participations, and sponsor capital commitments. The QIP alone accounted for ₹800 crore, with strong participation from marquee institutional investors. It signalled trust in our business model, our ability to deliver, and the long term direction we are building towards.

Our partnership with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL) also grew deeper. With a cumulative investment commitment of ₹1,800 crore, NYL now holds a 49% stake across our entire commercial portfolio, including upcoming mixed-use developments in Noida. Their partnership goes beyond capital. It is built on shared values, highest level of governance, aligned intent, and a belief in long-term value creation.

Together, these capital initiatives have fortified our balance sheet. As of March 31, 2025, we were net debt positive, with a cash surplus of ₹435 crore. This gives us the headroom to pursue new opportunities, manage risks with care, and continue scaling in a thoughtful, sustainable way.

Strengthening the Foundation for Execution at Scale

Our ability to deliver at scale is rooted in the strength of our people, structured processes, robust technology, and sound governance. This year, we onboarded over 120 professionals across functions, with focused hiring for the residential vertical. We also took steady steps toward building more inclusive teams, improving gender diversity across functions, and setting a clear target of 30% women’s representation over the next 24 months.

We partnered with In Tandem Global Consulting to co-author, “Concrete Change—A Study of the Economic Impact of Better Pay Parity & Inclusion of Women in Real Estate”. This is not just a milestone for the industry, but a reaffirmation of our belief that progress in business must go hand in hand with social progress.

To support consistent quality across projects, we institutionalised SOPs across 13 verticals of the real estate value chain. These were rigorously tested through internal audits to ensure operational rigour. Our digital roadmap continues to guide us across core functions, enabling greater project visibility, real-time decision-making, sharper operational efficiency, and enhanced stakeholder experience. We now use a suite of tools such as SAP, BIM, Salesforce, Zoho, and Autodesk to further strengthen our execution across the value chain.

On the sustainability front, we are working across the portfolio to conserve energy and water, reduce emissions, and minimise waste. We have already set reduction targets for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while actively baselining Scope 3 net zero targets.

On governance, we have continued to strengthen our Board with individuals who bring deep, cross sectoral expertise and strategic insight. Their guidance ensures disciplined capital allocation, thoughtful risk management, and a steady focus on long-term value creation. To deepen this focus, we welcomed Atul B. Lall, Ira Gupta, Malini Thadani, and Anthony Ramsey Malloy to our Board.

Together, they bring strength in building at scale, leadership, culture, investing, and sustainability. Their combined insight will help us with execution at scale, enable adoption of technology , and strengthen governance through disciplined capital allocation, thoughtful risk management, and a focus on long term value creation.

Creating Holistic Experiences with Purpose

At Max Estates, we believe real estate is about more than just structures. It is about the lived experiences and the wellbeing of the tenants. Our design-led, hospitality-driven approach brings our WorkWell and LiveWell philosophy to life, weaving in nature, community, wellness, and sustainability across all our offerings.

Sustainability remains central to who we are. This year, we secured LEED, WELL, and IGBC certifications across operational assets and are now working towards a 5-star GRESB rating in 2025. We are also aligning our net zero goals with the Science-Based Targets Initiative (SBTi) and have committed to reaching net zero emissions for both Scope 1 and Scope 2 by 2040.

The central forest courtyard at Max Square, spanning over 11,000 square feet serves as a living example of biophilia in commercial real estate. Through our in-house engagement vertical, Pulse, we hosted over 200 events, reaching more than 8,400 people and contributing to a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 6.9 out of 10.

Beyond business, we continue to invest in positive social impact. Through our partnership with Habitat for Humanity, we have provided over 25 homes to underprivileged workers in Rewari, with 25 more underway. Our collaboration with the Latika Roy Foundation has resulted in a 56,000-square-foot, universally accessible space, the “Centre for Inclusion and Influence”, reaffirming our commitment to inclusive growth.

We are building a culture that puts people at the centre, helping us shape a workforce that is future ready. From structured performance frameworks to leadership development and digital skilling, our initiatives are designed to support growth,

well-being, equity, and inclusion. With initiatives across leadership development, ESG integration, digital transformation, and holistic retention, we are nurturing a culture aligned with our vision, growth, and sustainability goals.

Looking Ahead: Ambition Meets Discipline

We are entering FY2026 with our eyes on growth, and our feet on firm ground. Our priorities are clear: grow pre-sales by 15–20%, and launch three new offerings—Estate 360, Delhi One, and Sector 105, adding at least 3 million square feet of fresh opportunities every year. We will continue to advance construction across ongoing projects, pursue financial closures for key mixed-use offerings, and deepen the use of digital systems and ESG best practices.

What we build says everything about who we are.

The path ahead calls for ambition, but also for care, clarity, and a commitment to doing right by the people and places we shape. At Max Estates, we believe our spaces should breathe. They should nurture, restore, and belong. Through every project, we stay committed to creating long-term value and improving quality of life, while placing wellbeing at the core. We are not just a real estate brand. We are here to craft offerings that inspire, empower, and enrich the lives of those who inhabit them.

To our investors, partners, customers, employees, and the larger ecosystem—thank you for standing with us, trusting us, and believing in what we are building. Together, we look ahead to a future rooted in wellbeing, shaped by intention, and made to last.

Established in 2016, Max Estates Limited is the real estate arm of Max Group. With a vision to bring real wellbeing to real estate, Max Estates has curated a diversified portfolio of Grade A sustainable residential and commercial developments. These span across asset classes and key locations in Delhi NCR.

Highlights of Our Journey

In just a few years, Max Estates has brought meaningful change to the real estate sector. Our Grade A developer-managed commercial buildings are built on our signature WorkWell philosophy. Backed by our track record in commercial development, along with a clear design language, a differentiated end-user experience, and the governance strength of Max Group, we are now scaling both residential and commercial portfolios to deliver long-term value to all stakeholders.

In 2023, we launched our first residential development, Estate 128. It was a landmark success and gained recognition as a redefined experience in the luxury segment. A year later, in 2024, we introduced Estate 360 in Gurugram. It was not only our first residential launch in the city, but also the first intergenerational offering of its kind in Delhi NCR.

FY2025 marked a period of strong growth. Our development portfolio expanded from 8 million square feet in FY2024 to over 17.1 million square feet. This included residential, commercial, and mixed use segments.

We also made a notable entry into the mixed-use space by acquiring prime land parcels and development rights across Delhi NCR. These moves reinforced our operational capabilities and deepened our presence in key growth corridors.

With our LiveWell and WorkWell philosophies at the core, Max Estates aims to add at least 3 million square feet to its portfolio every year. These philosophies guide how we design and operate in creating spaces for our customers.

As a wellbeing company enabled by real estate, Max Estates is committed to creating spaces that enable collaboration, innovation, and community.

These spaces go beyond being just functional and aesthetically pleasing. They are environmentally sustainable and designed to promote holistic wellness for the people who live and work in them.

ESG Strategy

In FY2025, we continued to evolve and take forward-looking steps that not only protected the environment but also placed people’s wellbeing at the centre of our work.

Design Interventions

We design our buildings to optimise environmental performance by working in harmony with nature. We maximise natural daylight in over 50% of occupied spaces and have adapted a biophilic design, with over 15% of each site dedicated to green cover for a strong connection to nature. Wellbeing and safety are key to our day-to-day operations. Our team carries out comfort surveys and health sessions to listen and respond to people’s wellbeing needs. Integrated Management Systems (IMS)

We embed sustainability into how we work every day through globally recognised IMS standards: ISO 9001 (Quality), ISO 14001 (Environmental), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety). These frameworks guide us to act responsibly, with both outcomes and processes shaped by care.

ISO 14001 helps us stay mindful of our environmental footprint by encouraging energy efficiency, reduced waste, conservation of natural resources, and thoughtful sourcing. We track our carbon footprint, keeping ourselves accountable to both our goals and our stakeholders.

ISO 45001 reflects our commitment to health, safety, and the wellbeing of our employees. A proactive risk management framework and ethical labour practices foster a culture where safety comes first, trust is built, and community relations are strengthened.

ISO 9001 ensures trust and safety through data integrity, strong internal controls, and continuous improvement. Standardised processes and clear responsibilities drive transparent governance, supporting alignment with global ESG reporting standards, such as the GRI, and enabling the tracking of measurable KPIs.

Strategic Benefits of IMS Implementation:

Strengthened Brand Reputation: Certifications reaffirm our commitment to high ESG standards, building stakeholder trust.

Investor Confidence: Robust, third-party validated systems bring transparency, aligning us with sustainable investment mandates.

Operational Efficiency: With one framework, we can anticipate risks, manage costs prudently, and deliver consistent quality.

Regulatory Compliance: IMS streamlines alignment to national and international regulations, helping us stay resilient in an evolving landscape.

Risk and Compliance

We uphold a strong commitment to environmental compliance and risk mitigation, particularly in alignment with evolving regulatory frameworks. During FY2025, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) enforced the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana during the winter months to address rising pollution levels. In adherence to these directives, Max Estates temporarily halted construction activities at select sites to prevent environmental degradation. While this led to short-term delays in construction timelines, it reflected our commitment to sustainable and responsible development.

Our sites were also reviewed under the Environment (Protection) Act. Every observation was met with care and swift action, and we remained fully compliant with the applicable legal and environmental standards.

Climate Risk and Scenario Analysis

We recognise that climate change poses real challenges to real estate assets. These risks range from acute weather events to long-term shifts in climate patterns. These changes affect how resilient our assets are and how we continue to build confidence among our stakeholders.

Physical Climate Risks

We know that climate change is no longer a distant concern, it is shaping the way we live and work today. Our portfolios are also exposed to climate-related risks, including extreme heat, flooding, and erratic rainfall, especially in the Delhi NCR region, which, according to the State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC), faces high vulnerability due to unplanned urbanisation and rising temperatures. #### OPERATING ENVIRONMENT

Max Estates operates in a dynamic real estate environment influenced by various macroeconomic, demographic, and technological factors. With a deep understanding of these trends and the business needs they create, we have positioned ourselves to respond to evolving trends and fresh opportunities, particularly in the Delhi NCR region, through a dynamic approach in strategy

Despite global uncertainties, India’s macroeconomic landscape showed resilience in 2024, staying on track as one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated a Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 6.5%1. Strong domestic demand, ongoing infrastructure development, and easing inflation supported this momentum.

As global uncertainties continue, trade tensions and supply chain issues, and the announcement of new global tariffs by the United States may impact the external sector. The US has introduced a 10%2 universal tariff on imports. While India has a temporary exemption from the additional 26%3, we still face the baseline 10% duty on exports.

At home, the Union Budget’s tax incentives could boost GDP by 0.6-0.7%. Lower inflation, stable oil prices, and reduced borrowing rates are expected to enhance both spending and investment.

Looking ahead to FY2026, India’s outlook remains steady. Structural reforms, a growing workforce, and increased global interest in manufacturing continue to support momentum. Inflation is projected to ease to 4.0%4, while GDP growth is expected to remain steady at 6.5%5, as per the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)6.

The Indian real estate sector is poised for significant growth. It is projected to reach $1 trillion7 by 2030 and $7–10 trillion by 2047. Growth is driven by expanding infrastructure, rapid urbanisation, a young population, a growing manufacturing base, new jobs, and a sharper focus on sustainability and technology. The sector’s contribution to GDP is expected to stay steady at 6–8%. Government policies, such as the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), add to the momentum. The residential market is seeing healthy demand across all segments, while strong leasing demand supports commercial real estate, led by Global Capability Centres (GCCs) that span multiple sectors,

Max Estates is guided by the belief that people thrive when they LiveWell and WorkWell. With this philosophy at the core, we are well-positioned for sustainable growth in Delhi NCR. We benefit from a strong economic environment, a committed team of over 200 full-time professionals, technology-led operations, and a diversified portfolio across residential, commercial, and mixed-use segments.

Pre-sales performance has been strong. With Estate 128 completely sold out and Estate 360 nearing full capacity at 96%, we are gearing up for our next chapter of growth. To support this, we secured ₹800 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement, along with an additional ₹150 crore from preferential allotments to promoters and strategic investors.

Our long-term partnership with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL) Insurance includes a total investment commitment of ₹1,800 crore, with ₹550 crore earmarked for upcoming projects in Delhi One and Sector 105, Noida. As of March 31, 2025, Max Estates is net debt-positive with a healthy cash surplus of ₹435 crore. This provides the headroom to explore fresh opportunities and grow with discipline. Favourable urbanisation trends, changing consumer preferences and and strong policy support further reinforce our outlook. Max Estates is well-equipped to navigate macroeconomic uncertainties and continue its momentum through FY2026 and beyond.
